message:
unknown, I can only speak for myself when I say that I have had nothing but bad experiences with the reps at Correctional Billing Services/T-Netix/Evercom/Securus.  The hold times are ridiculous but what is worse is to be spoken to as if I am both stupid and just an annoyance to the "customer service" rep.  This has happened with each of my several calls to them.

The customer service reps have told me a different story each time I call them.  I must call them regularly as CBS puts a block on my phone before they bill me, each and every time, and each and every time I've called I get different explanations and different directions from these csr's.   Having been in customer service myself, I am particularly polite when dealing with csr's but that does not get me the same treatment in return when dealing with the CBS/T-Netix/Evercom/Securus crowd.  My last call resulted in the rep insisting my loved one is being held somewhere other than where he really is, and she insisted that from now on my calls would be $11.00+ per call.  I informed her that the recording always says "the cost for this call will be $.85, thank you for using T-Netix" and that if I start being charged $11.00 per call when the recording says I'll be charged $.85 then that would be illegal, and that I also will take steps if the charges suddenly change after this particular call to CBS with her.  I was civil and polite throughout being spoken to like I was dirt, and when  I made it clear I would not simply accept my calls jumping from $.85 to $11.00 and that my loved one isn't even in the prison they say he is in she actually started yelling "What the  did you just say to me?" followed by more cussing directed at me.  I asked for her name and she hung up on me.   Sorry, I can't at this point feel anything but disgust for anyone associated with any of the T-Netix/Evercom/Securus/CBS monster.   I do however remain civil at least, which is more than I get in return.

Another point of interest is that she told me that I have a limit of $240.00 that I can spend on calls in a 90 day period, and that even if I keep everything paid up, if I go over $240.00 worth of calls in 90 days, I will get a block put on my line.  Also, if I should use up the $240.00 say in the first 30 days, even if I keep it paid up to date, a block will be put on my line  from when the cycle started.  What the heck for?  If I'm paying for the calls why block the line at some limit they picked for my phone usage?  If I'm paid up, there is no excuse for that!
